source.note: Initial file made by bench/cost/initial-measured.mjs from the 2026-11-01 runs (CF-REPORT.md); none re-checked yet.

editDoReq.how: Cloudflare's analytics for the room, divided by the edits in the run; includes each party's connect and the room's alarms, so it slightly over-counts.

editRowsWritten.how: Rows the room wrote (Cloudflare's analytics), divided by the edits in the run.

editRowsRead.how: Rows the room read (Cloudflare's analytics), divided by the edits in the run.

editGBs.how: The room's active time in the run (Cloudflare's analytics) × 128 MB, divided by the edits; the room hibernates between messages.

editWorkerCpuMs.how: Edits travel over the open WebSocket straight to the room: no Worker runs for them.

editArchiveRowsWritten.how: Once a project passes 10,000 changes, each old change is moved to a compressed archive file and its row deleted; Cloudflare bills a delete as a row written.

connWorkerReq.how: One Worker request: the WebSocket upgrade, after the token check.

connWorkerCpuMs.how: The Worker's median CPU per request in the live-sync runs was about 3 ms (token check and hand-off to the room).

connDoReq.how: Cloudflare: "A request is needed to create a WebSocket connection." Billed in full, not 20:1.

connRowsWritten.how: A hello arms the room's upkeep alarm: its due time is one row, and Cloudflare bills each setAlarm as one row written.

connGBs.how: A hello wakes the room for about as long as an edit does (≈ 15 ms × 128 MB).

connRowsRead.how: The hello reads the project's branches, people and the changes the client missed; a short absence reads a few dozen rows.

presenceMsgPerSecWhileDragging.how: Carton's client sends at most 10 presence messages a second (PRESENCE_PER_SEC); the Cardboard app's pages send at most 1 a second while you click or type, so 10 is the upper bound.

presenceDoReq.how: Each presence message is one incoming WebSocket message to the room; it's relayed to the others and never stored.

presenceGBs.how: About 1.6 ms of room time per message (no storage write) × 128 MB.

presenceAlarmPerHour.how: While someone shows presence, the room checks every 60 s (half the 120 s timeout) for sockets gone silent; counted per person-hour, an upper bound when teammates overlap.

upkeepAlarmPerHour.how: The room's upkeep (archiving old changes, sweeping expired envelopes) is due an hour after an edit or a hello, so at most one an editing hour per project.

alarmRowsWritten.how: Cloudflare bills each setAlarm() as one row written.

alarmGBs.how: An alarm wakes the room for a few milliseconds × 128 MB.

idleDoReqPerHour.how: Keepalive pings are answered by Cloudflare's auto-response without waking the room, and Cloudflare's pricing page says those aren't charged.

idleGBsPerHour.how: An idle room hibernates; Cloudflare doesn't bill duration while it does.

idleRowsWrittenPerHour.how: Nothing is stored while nobody edits.

gbWorkerReq.how: 8 MiB parts: 128 part uploads plus the checks, manifest, start and finish of the upload.

gbWorkerCpuMs.how: After fix/cf-stream-parts the lab measured 3–9 ms of CPU per part (32 parts, one 256 MB run): about 6 ms × 140 requests. Before the fix: 61–359 ms per part.

gbR2ClassA.how: Per 8 MiB part: the upload itself and three small records (lock, marker, release); plus starting and finishing the upload.

gbR2ClassB.how: About one read per part (the upload's lock), plus the checks before it starts.

gbDoReq.how: None with R2. With the optional daily write cap switched on, one per part (its counter).

gbVaultDoReq.how: Without R2, each part goes to the vault Durable Object, plus the copy when the upload finishes.

gbVaultRowsWritten.how: The vault stores 1 MiB per row: each MiB written as a part, copied once when the upload completes, and the part rows deleted.

gbVaultGBs.how: The vault was active about 26 s for a 100 MB upload on the good profile (Cloudflare's analytics, one run).

segWorkerReq.how: Per preview segment the client checks the object, any damage report and the manifest, then writes the manifest, the bytes and the stream's list entry (upload.ts, stream.ts).

segWorkerCpuMs.how: Small requests that stream through: about 2 ms in all (estimate).

segR2ClassA.how: Three writes per segment: the manifest, the bytes and the list entry.

segR2ClassB.how: Three checks per segment: the object, a damage report and the manifest.

segVaultDoReq.how: Without R2, each of the segment's six calls is a request to the vault.

segVaultRowsWritten.how: The bytes (one 1 MiB row), the manifest, the list entry and the object's record.

viewWorkerReqPerMiB.how: A teammate reads each 2 s segment (≈ 0.48 MiB at 2 Mbit/s) and its list entry: two requests per segment. Played media is cached on their disk, so replays are free.

viewVaultRowsReadPerMiB.how: Without R2, the vault reads one 1 MiB row per segment.

viewVaultGBsPerMiB.how: Without R2, the vault is awake about 80 ms per MiB it serves (estimate).

changeBytes.how: A change row in the room's database until it's archived; the newest 10,000 stay in the room.

limits.value: 10 ms of CPU per request on Workers Free (5 minutes on Paid)
limits.observed: Upload parts were read whole into memory: 61–359 ms of CPU each. After a burst Cloudflare stopped them with error 1102 (HTTP 503), so a 1 GB upload never finished. With fix/cf-stream-parts: 3–9 ms per part, 32 of 32 parts ok.
limits.carton: A clear error, 4 retries with backoff, then a stop the upload can resume from. The fix streams each part straight to storage (branch fix/cf-stream-parts, not yet merged).

limits.value: 128 MB of memory per Worker isolate
limits.observed: A 96 MiB part failed (HTTP 503) while another upload shared the isolate; a 99 MiB part alone passed.
limits.carton: The same retry path. Streaming parts (fix/cf-stream-parts) never holds a part in memory.

limits.value: 100 MB per request body (Free and Pro plans)
limits.observed: A 101 MiB part was refused at Cloudflare's edge with HTTP 413; 64, 96 and 99 MiB passed.
limits.carton: Upload parts are 8–64 MiB, so a file would need to be over 640 GiB (10,000 parts) to come near it.

limits.observed: A raw 33 MiB frame: Cloudflare closed the socket (code 1009). The room closes 1009 above its own 24 MiB cap.
limits.carton: Changes over 1 MiB travel as uploaded envelopes (5 MiB: 2.0–3.5 s, 20 MiB: 3.9–5.1 s). A 30 MiB change is refused on your machine as "too large" in 215 ms, and the next edit still goes through.

limits.value: 50 subrequests per request on Free (1,000 to Cloudflare's own services); 10,000 on Paid
limits.observed: R2 calls count against the 1,000, not the 50. Checking 200 files at once worked (4.1 s); asked for 1,000, the server answered 200 per call (9.4 s).
limits.carton: The server checks at most 200 files per request (BLOB_HEADS_PER_REQUEST) and the client asks again for the rest.

limits.value: 2 MB per database row in a Durable Object
limits.observed: Not hit: the vault stores media in 1 MiB rows.
limits.carton: Media without R2 is cut into 1 MiB rows; changes over 1 MiB go as envelopes.

limits.value: 100,000 Worker requests a day on Free (resets 00:00 UTC)
limits.observed: Not tested directly (it needed a late-night window and approval). A client whose session was refused retried 86 times a minute, about 2 requests per try: ≈ 245,000 a day from one stuck client, 2.5× the limit.
limits.carton: Past it, Cloudflare answers error 1027 until midnight UTC and nobody can connect. fix/cf-reconnect-backoff slows retries to 15 s, or 5 minutes while the session is refused (not yet merged).

limits.value: 100,000 Durable Object requests a day on Free
limits.observed: Not tested (the lab stayed under 50% of every daily limit; it used 5,409 on its busiest day).
limits.carton: Past it, edits and uploads fail until midnight UTC; Carton keeps them on your machine and sends them when it can.

limits.value: 13,000 GB-s of Durable Object time a day on Free
limits.observed: Not tested (the lab used 28 GB-s on its busiest day).
limits.carton: As above: requests fail until midnight UTC.

limits.value: 100,000 rows written a day on Free (5 million read)
limits.observed: Not tested (the lab wrote 14,983 rows on its busiest day).
limits.carton: The room archives old changes in batches from an alarm, never on an edit, because each archived row costs one more row written.

limits.value: 5 GB of Durable Object storage in total on Free
limits.observed: Not hit (12.7 MB used). The vault has no sweep for abandoned uploads, so their parts stay and count against it.
limits.carton: Without R2, all media sits in Durable Objects, so a solo editor's footage alone can pass 5 GB. Keep media in R2.

limits.value: R2: 10 GB-month of storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B a month free
limits.observed: The lab used 993 Class A and 698 Class B this month. A bucket lifecycle rule deletes test files and aborts unfinished uploads after a day.
limits.carton: Past it, R2 bills (it never stops). Its free amounts are monthly, not daily.

limits.value: Not a Cloudflare limit: a link that dies without closing
limits.observed: Through a 5-minute outage the socket stayed "open": status "Syncing", no offline event. 66 edits made offline, 0 lost; they all arrived 66.5 s after the link came back, on TCP's retransmission timer.
limits.carton: fix/cf-dead-link closes a link whose keepalive goes unanswered for 15 s, so the app shows offline and reconnects at once (not yet merged).

notes.workersFree: Workers Free: 100,000 requests a day, 10 ms of CPU per request, no fee. Requests to static assets are free and unlimited.
notes.doFree: Durable Objects on Workers Free (SQLite-backed only): 100,000 requests, 13,000 GB-s, 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written a day; 5 GB stored in total.
notes.ws: A request is needed to create a WebSocket connection. For billing only, a 20:1 ratio is applied to incoming WebSocket messages; outgoing messages and incoming protocol pings aren't charged; auto-responses (setWebSocketAutoResponse) aren't charged.
notes.alarm: Each setAlarm() is billed as a single row written; deletes are counted as rows written.
notes.duration: Duration bills the 128 MB a Durable Object is allocated, whatever it uses; an object that is idle and eligible for hibernation isn't billed for duration.
notes.r2: R2 bills on either Workers plan; its free amounts are monthly and apply to Standard storage only. Storage is the average of each day's peak over the month. Egress is free. DeleteObject and AbortMultipartUpload are free.
notes.dailyReset: Workers Free daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
